Genus-three example from Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó, *Heegaard Floer homology*,
Example 2.1.13 and Figure 2.5 (author PDF dated 2024-08-20):
<https://web.math.princeton.edu/~szabo/HeegaardBook.pdf>.
The twelve octahedron edges become three β curves under reflection gluing.
Every β meets two different α curves. This is not a disjoint union of
genus-one layouts or a trivial stabilization.

```{julia}
using Topology
const H = Topology.Heegaard
const ROOT = dirname(Base.active_project())
diagram = H.certify_heegaard(H.load_heegaard(joinpath(ROOT, "test", "fixtures", "t3_octahedron_v1.hgd.json")))
feasible = H.load_layout(joinpath(ROOT, "test", "fixtures", "t3_octahedron_v1.hgd.layout.json"), diagram)
(genus = H.surface_genus(diagram), homology = H.first_homology(diagram))
```

## Before

The saved feasible seed starts from the source octahedron's planar embedding.
An explicit annular half-twist and two local inverse disk spins place its
six disks in the standard two rows without changing cyclic port order.
This is a source-specific construction, not a claim of a complete router.

```{julia}
H.plot(feasible)
```

## After

The same fixed-100 Julia relaxation used by the website, with normal exits.

```{julia}
figure = H.plot(diagram, feasible)
figure
```

```{julia}
(valid = figure.report.valid, crossings = length(figure.crossings),
 stop_reason = figure.backend_trace["smoothing"]["stop_reason"],
 source_hash = figure.diagram_hash)
```

Source incidence is transcribed; curve orientations and intersection IDs are
explicit local choices. The genus and homology above are computed checks,
not independent evidence of every source convention. The solver does not
claim a global optimum.
